rows.title: Eyes
rows.text: Jumping spiders have eight simple eyes, and you very likely have eight as well. In the bold jumping spider, the two big front eyes can follow a moving target only with guidance from the smaller eyes at the side. Nobody has measured what each of your eyes does unless you are a bold jumping spider.
rows.note: Left out the telephoto optics (R4, Plexippus validus only) and the vestigial rear eyes (R5, Lyssomanes only) to keep the row short.

rows.title: Sharpness
rows.text: For most jumping spiders, nobody has measured how sharply you see. If you are a Phidippus johnsoni, your big front eyes see about an eighth of the detail a human sees, and you very likely share that with other Phidippus spiders. If you are a bold jumping spider, the light-sensing cells in the sharpest zone of each of your side eyes sit about half a degree apart.
rows.note: R3's quote gives 0.13 degrees, not 3.8 cycles a degree; the eighth rests on the record value 3.8 against 30 for a human. R2 and R4/R5 left out.

rows.title: Field of view
rows.text: If you are a bold jumping spider, each of the eyes just beside your two big front eyes sees about 70 degrees from side to side and about 100 degrees from top to bottom. The only other measurement is a side-to-side span of about 100 degrees for those eyes in Menemerus semilimbatus, a gray wall jumping spider's relative. Nobody has measured the rest, including how far the fields of your two eyes overlap.
rows.note: Left out R8 (25 degree overlap, family-level, grade g) and R3/R4/R6/R7 (retina size of the front eyes, not a field of view); optics do not carry beyond the genus.

rows.title: Eye movement
rows.text: Inside each of your two big front eyes, the retina moves, scanning across what you look at. If you are a bold jumping spider, your front eyes scan a still shape the same way with or without the eyes beside them, but they rely on those eyes to find and track a moving one. Nobody has measured this in most other jumping spiders, so nobody knows how closely you match the bold jumping spider.
rows.note: Left out the fovea and the Marpissa priming and Salticidae dwell-time records to keep the row short and tied to the one measured species.

rows.title: Color
rows.text: If you are a regal jumping spider, your big front eyes have three kinds of color-sensing cell, and one kind senses ultraviolet. If you are a Plexippus validus, you have only two kinds, green and ultraviolet, and if you are a Habronattus pyrrithrix, you have three, with the red-sensing kind in a small patch at the center of the eye. Nobody has measured how many kinds you have if you are any other jumping spider.
rows.note: Left out the carried wavelength peaks and the 300-700 nm lens range because no number had a clear job; the orange/blue grating result (R12) is from Evarcha and was not stated.

rows.title: Movement
rows.text: When something moves near you, you turn to face it. If you are a bold jumping spider, your big front eyes scan differently when dots move like a living animal than when they move in other ways. If you are a magnolia green jumping spider, the retinas of your side eyes are less refined for sensing motion than those of the other jumping spiders studied, and for most species nobody has measured how well you see movement.
rows.note: Left out the turning speeds (R14) and the 16 degrees per second figure (R15): the records are for the family and the quotes do not name a species, so they cannot be pinned to one.

rows.title: Vibration and sound
rows.text: If you are a bold jumping spider, a low tone in the air makes you freeze, even when it comes from more than 3 meters away, and a shaking surface under your feet is unpleasant enough that you learn to avoid whatever you were looking at. If you are a brilliant jumping spider, the rate of a courting male's vibrations is an important part of whether he wins a mate. Nobody has measured what most other jumping spiders sense of sound or vibration.
rows.note: Left out R1 (record names Corythalia canosa, list says Anasaitis canosa) and R3 (about courting signals sent, not sensed).
